behavior.explanation: The visible behavior is conditional on verified role, file lookup result, request branch, bypass configuration, and downstream vector-save behavior. The input authorization object is the selected file identified by file_id. The principal output effect, when not bypassed, is a vector write to collection_name, which is a separate resource; the same selected file is also updated with content/status/hash and, on success, collection_name metadata. No shown process_file check establishes that the caller owns the destination collection.

branches.condition: Caller has role user, and get_file_by_id_and_user_id(form_data.file_id, user.id, db=db) returns the file.
branches.explanation: The caller-owned file proceeds to one of the content, existing-collection, or normal file-processing branches. If bypass is true, vector saving is skipped after the selected file is updated. Otherwise the endpoint passes the documents and collection_name to save_docs_to_vector_db and, on a truthy result, updates the selected file as completed.

branches.condition: Caller has role user, and the supplied file_id identifies a file not returned by the file_id-plus-caller-user-id lookup.
branches.explanation: The selected file is absent on this visible path, so process_file raises HTTP 404 before document processing, file updates, or vector saving. The exact helper implementation semantics remain a bounded source gap, although the endpoint's call is explicitly file_id plus user.id.

branches.condition: Caller has role admin, and get_file_by_id(form_data.file_id, db=db) returns another user's file.
branches.explanation: The shown admin lookup has no user-id predicate and therefore can select the file. The endpoint then processes and updates that selected file and may write to the supplied/default destination collection. This is an admin role exception, not evidence that an ordinary user may process another user's file.

branches.condition: A non-null form_data.collection_name is supplied and embedding/retrieval is not bypassed.
branches.explanation: The supplied collection_name is passed to save_docs_to_vector_db with add=True. The shown process_file path contains no check comparing the destination collection owner with caller, file.user_id, or any other principal. Whether the downstream helper or vector backend imposes an independent ownership or access check is unresolved here.

branches.condition: form_data.collection_name is null.
branches.explanation: The endpoint sets collection_name to file-{file.id}. This default is derived from the selected input file, but it is still a collection resource and is not thereby proven to have the same authorization or owner as the file.

branches.condition: form_data.content is truthy.
branches.explanation: The endpoint builds a document from the supplied content, attempts to delete collection file-{file.id}, and later updates the selected file. The supplied destination collection_name remains the value passed to the later vector-save call unless bypass returns first.

branches.condition: BYPASS_EMBEDDING_AND_RETRIEVAL is true after file processing.
branches.explanation: The endpoint updates the selected file to completed, updates its hash, returns collection_name None, and does not call save_docs_to_vector_db.

The downstream vector backend operations used by save_docs_to_vector_db were not closed for authorization semantics; no conclusion here establishes or rules out a backend-level destination ownership check.

observations.subject: process_file entry
observations.claim: The shown endpoint is POST /process/file and selects a file using an admin-wide lookup for admin callers or an ID-plus-user lookup for non-admin callers before processing branches.

observations.subject: verified caller
observations.claim: The endpoint dependency get_verified_user admits only users whose role is user or admin and returns that user object; the endpoint then branches on user.role.

observations.subject: POST /process/file process_file
observations.claim: The endpoint obtains a verified user, selects a file using either an admin-wide file_id lookup or a non-admin file_id-plus-user-id lookup, then processes the selected file and may update file metadata and save documents to the supplied or default collection.

observations.subject: caller
observations.claim: get_verified_user permits only roles user or admin and returns that user object; process_file uses the returned user's role and, for the non-admin lookup, the returned user's id.

observations.subject: supplied file_id
observations.claim: For admin callers, the endpoint calls get_file_by_id(form_data.file_id, db=db), whose shown implementation performs a direct database lookup by id without a user-id predicate. For non-admin callers, the endpoint calls get_file_by_id_and_user_id(form_data.file_id, user.id, db=db); the helper body is shown in the catalog but its semantic extraction was not completed in this bounded run.

observations.subject: destination collection
observations.claim: The destination is form_data.collection_name when supplied; otherwise it defaults to file-{file.id}. The endpoint passes this value to save_docs_to_vector_db, and when an explicit collection_name is supplied it passes add=True. No destination-owner check is visible in the shown process_file source.

observations.subject: file selection
observations.claim: If the selected file is absent, the endpoint raises HTTP 404 and does not enter the processing branches. A non-admin caller therefore reaches processing only when the file lookup constrained by that caller's identity returns a file; an admin caller reaches processing for any file returned by the id-only lookup.

observations.subject: selected file
observations.claim: After document preparation, the endpoint writes text_content into the selected file, computes a hash, and later updates status, collection_name metadata, and hash on that same selected file. On errors it marks that file failed and clears its hash.

observations.subject: vector output
observations.claim: When embedding/retrieval is not bypassed and save_docs_to_vector_db returns truthy, the endpoint treats the vector save as successful and records the destination collection_name on the selected file. The vector effect targets the destination collection, which is a distinct resource from the input file; the shown endpoint does not bind destination ownership to the caller.

observations.subject: BYPASS_EMBEDDING_AND_RETRIEVAL
observations.claim: When request.app.state.config.BYPASS_EMBEDDING_AND_RETRIEVAL is true, the endpoint updates the selected file to completed and stores its hash, returns collection_name None, and returns before calling save_docs_to_vector_db; this is a successful file-processing path without the vector-write effect.

sourceBindings.claim: The endpoint receives its caller from the framework dependency get_verified_user; the shown function uses that object as user and passes user.id to the non-admin file lookup, while passing user to the loader and vector-save call.

The input file resource is selected by form_data.file_id and resolved to file; for non-admin callers the shown endpoint requests a file matching both that ID and user.id, while admins request by file ID alone.

The destination resource is collection_name from form_data, or the derived value file-{file.id} when collection_name is None; the shown endpoint passes this value to vector-database operations without an ownership check in this function.

rules.claim: POST /process/file enters process_file with request, form_data, a verified user, and an async database session.

The vector-save helper first queries the destination collection by the supplied document hash; if an existing document has a different file_id, it raises a duplicate-content error, while a matching file_id is treated as a re-add/reindex.

The helper checks whether the supplied collection_name already exists. With overwrite false and add false, an existing collection causes an immediate successful return without inserting new items; otherwise processing continues to embedding and insertion.

Exceptions from vector saving propagate back to the route's outer handler, which updates the selected file status to failed and clears its hash before returning an HTTP 400-style error; this is a file-side failure update, not destination authorization.

guided-evidence-v2 local interface: controlDelta is {schemaVersion:"authorization-control-update/v1",rules:[],sourceBindings:[],dependencies:[],premiseValues:[],policyRules:[],atomic?:false,baseRevision?:current revision}. Submit just changed items, not the entire graph.
Each item has op:add|replace, questionId, targetKey. Replace names the current same-question target; a model reason is optional for ordinary items, and the host records explicit replacement provenance and revisionOf. Dependency reason remains required to explain source relevance. baseRevision detects a stale view. atomic:true applies the submitted group or none: its own or newly broken predecessor/dependency links cause rollback; unrelated unchanged gaps remain visible without rolling back this transaction. Rejected items and their dependent gaps remain visible; correct only diagnosed items.
To abandon a malformed UNACCEPTED draft, submit withdrawals:[{group:rules|sourceBindings|dependencies|premiseValues|policyRules,questionId,targetKey,reason}]. This retires only that exact draft's current rejection, preserving its original proposal and the withdrawal reason. It never deletes an accepted target, another group's error, source invalidation or missing predecessor/dependency gaps. Failed atomic updates apply no withdrawals. Renaming a draft alone does not withdraw it.
rules are entry/guard/reject/continue/effect with pathKey,after,evidenceIds,claim and optional finite condition/principal/resource/operation/authorizedBy/complete. sourceBindings are source identities with pathKey,after,evidenceIds,claim,bindingKey,bindingKind; the host sets kind:binding. A source identity is never a user value.
A new entry with omitted after declares a root (after:[]). Explicit entry predecessors stay unchanged. Replacements and all other rule kinds require after; a missing predecessor must never be guessed. Final observations may be omitted when there are no additional observations.
premiseValues are explicit user facts: {op,questionId,targetKey,status:known,value,text:<exact original user span>} or {op,questionId,targetKey,status:unspecified,text}. Unspecified has NO value field; it does not mean null or false. Omit unspecified items if no update is needed. Policy mappings stay in policyRules, with expected,text,location and optional condition; the host sets origin:policy.
For a shown ambiguous WorkItem submit workSelections:[{questionId,itemId,candidateId}] using its shown candidate ID. This is a lexical read choice, not an authorization fact or a closed-state declaration. Atomic applies to the control update groups; location choices are separate read intents.
Current locationTasks contain unlocated WorkItems or optional unconfirmed lexical references from interpreted parent source, not source interpretations. For select-candidate submit controlDelta.workSelections:[{questionId,itemId,candidateId}] using the exact same-question shown IDs; this is a read intent, not a claim that the helper is relevant. For locate use ordinary source_search/source_symbol/source_read to establish an original location. A location task does not authorize localExtractions until its actual read window is offered as an explanation task. Resolve decisive locations alongside already-read explanation tasks; unresolved decisive locations cannot be skipped as completed questions. Optional lexical leads need not apply.
Current local explanation tasks are executable duties: interpret the offered WorkItem using its original sourceWindows and current question/premises. A read/citation alone does not settle its meaning.
Submit controlDelta.localExtractions:[{itemId,rules?,sourceBindings?,dependencies?,premiseValues?,policyRules?}]. Use op:add|replace,targetKey and the semantic fields of the corresponding local group, but OMIT questionId and evidenceIds inside these items: the host binds them to this offered WorkItem and actual current windows. It also supplies binding kind, origins and replacement digest. Keep after/from/parent as explicit current target keys; they express your proposed execution relationship, never lexical equality.
WorkItem.kind names a duty, not a rules.kind value. Principal-binding and resource-binding duties belong in sourceBindings with bindingKey and the appropriate bindingKind:principal or resource. The complete sourceBindings bindingKind enum is principal|resource|permission|configuration|value; rules.kind is entry|guard|reject|continue|effect. Use distinct targetKey values for distinct nodes across rules/sourceBindings. Reuse one typed principal/resource identity string for the same actual source object across bindings, guards and effects; use distinct identities for distinct objects. The host does not infer object aliases from prose or convert objects into identity strings.
Explain source conditions with the finite typed predicate algebra. Preserve owner=null separately from owner unspecified, missing grants separately from known false, and role exceptions. Check that claim text and typed predicate describe the same source branch before submitting. Source code does not supply a user premise. If a related source cannot be read, declare the dependency and its concrete gap rather than guessing.
Unknown premise entries are optional: normally omit them and keep the corresponding predicate binding unresolved. If submitting status:unspecified, text must be a verbatim span of the current question/premises, including its actual punctuation; do not paraphrase it. Prefer the default per-item update so an unrelated invalid span does not discard useful source interpretation. Request atomic:true only for a change that must succeed as one transaction.
A condition means THIS NODE IS REACHED. For source "if (!allowed) return deny; performEffect()", propose a reject terminal with condition allowed==false and an effect terminal with condition allowed==true on distinct pathKeys. Both conditions use wrapped operands. The effect follows the entry/bindings and any successful control, never the terminating reject. A guard reached on a failing condition cannot authorize its succeeding effect. Include explicit principal/resource binding nodes among the control/effect predecessors; identifying the same object in prose is insufficient.
An entry read does not close its called authorization helpers or upstream endpoint controls. Interpret the entry first, name decisive source dependencies, then interpret their actual windows and link the resulting conditions. Mark a terminal complete only after its relevant reachable controls and dependencies are examined. Policy pathKey must match the actual proposed behavior path, with expected outcome mapped from independent policy rather than source.
Unconfirmed lexical references are optional location leads, not compulsory explanation tasks. Link a dependency from the actual source rule when relevant to this question, or choose a shown candidate to inspect it. A unique same-name definition alone does not establish relevance or receiver identity.
Local explanation joins the next ordinary structured/native step. It does not create an extra provider request. You may still use ordinary changed control groups for already shown source outside an offered fragment. Invalid local items remain diagnosed while good siblings are retained, subject to the requested atomic update.
An interpreted source item remains editable until its question is checked. Amend existingTargets with op:replace when correcting the same source rule; a model reason may explain the change, otherwise the host records explicit local replacement provenance. Dependency relevance reasons remain required. Renaming a mistaken rule does not withdraw it. For an abandoned unaccepted draft, use root controlDelta.withdrawals with its exact group,questionId,targetKey and reason; accepted targets and missing links cannot be erased. After a stale local envelope rejection, use a currently offered task or a valid same-question ordinary update; specific rejected target diagnostics require correction or an explicit eligible withdrawal.
Domain feedback rejectedTargets shows at most four current rejected drafts with their exact group/question/target, submitted data, original local scope, diagnostics and archive pointer. Unaccepted targets require a corrected op:add under the same key; op:replace requires an accepted same-group target. A group conflict requires correcting the group or choosing a distinct key. Correct the fields named by diagnostics; pathKey, after, binding identity, conditions and completeness remain your explicit source interpretation. For local submission use only a CURRENTLY offered itemId and omit questionId/evidenceIds. Otherwise use the ordinary group with the recorded questionId and actually shown evidenceIds. If abandoning an eligible unaccepted draft, explicitly withdraw its exact identity with a reason. Renaming alone leaves the failure active. Large drafts are omitted as a whole with an archive pointer, never silently truncated or filled.
Deferred tasks are not current local offers. Whole original windows are selected within sourceBudget; no source lines or semantic fields are summarized. Previously shown evidence remains referenceable through the catalog and ordinary updates. A candidateRefinement location task offers the SAME indexed alternatives for an incompletely read entry; choose a narrower candidate only when it identifies this requested entry. The host does not change that choice or infer relevance.
A source binding's bindingKey declares its typed identity; principal/resource fields reference that bindingKey. For example bindingKind:principal,bindingKey:visitor declares visitor, and a downstream principal:visitor references it. On that binding node omit its own principal or repeat principal:visitor; principal:anotherName does not declare an alias. Use different typed identity keys for different objects even if labels/IDs match. authorizedBy asserts that a particular guard controls THIS effect on the same principal/resource; omit the assertion if no such linkage is established, and explain source-visible missing control rather than inventing a guard. Do not assume a checked input object also authorizes an output object.
Predicates support only {op:eq|neq,left:{binding:name}|{literal:scalar},right:{binding:name}|{literal:scalar}}, {op:is-null,value:{binding:name}|{literal:scalar}}, {op:all|any,args:[predicates]}, {op:not,arg:predicate}; scalar is string/number/boolean/null. BOTH operands must be wrapped, for example {op:"eq",left:{binding:"flag"},right:{literal:false}}; bare right:false is invalid. Max depth12/nodes64. No target code, arbitrary operator or natural text is evaluated. Only known premiseValues from exact current user spans enter evaluation; mapping meaning remains unreviewed. For an unspecified/unknown/not-given value OMIT the binding completely and refer to its key only in predicates; NEVER use value:null or value:false as an unknown placeholder. null is valid only when the current user explicitly supplies a null premise. Represent source outcomes with rules/conditions, do not invent user binding values from source.

Host uses a lexical location index, not a semantic call graph. Ambiguous candidates require an explicit pathHint/candidateId revision; missing/outside/dynamic facts stay local gaps. Place a dependency after a reject only if source order actually makes it unreachable. After an automatic read, incorporate the returned original evidence into a linked rule before calling a decisive dependency checked.
Policy mappings are separate candidates: {op,targetKey,questionId,pathKey,expected:allow|deny,origin:policy,text:<exact policy span>,location:<current independent location>,condition?}. Map only the supplied policy, do not derive it from implementation. Each live path needs a mapping for a determined policy assessment; incomplete mappings remain undetermined while behavior is deliverable. Formal policy mapping is still unreviewed.
For unspecified values, retain alternative feasible outcomes and name the missing fact. Local extraction and mapping meaning remain unreviewed.

For select-candidate submit controlDelta.workSelections:[{questionId,itemId,candidateId}] using the exact same-question shown IDs; this is a read intent, not a claim that the helper is relevant. For locate use ordinary source_search/source_symbol/source_read to establish an original location. A location task does not authorize localExtractions until its actual read window is offered as an explanation task. Resolve decisive locations alongside already-read explanation tasks; unresolved decisive locations cannot be skipped as completed questions. Optional lexical leads need not apply.
Current local explanation tasks are executable duties: interpret the offered WorkItem using its original sourceWindows and current question/premises. A read/citation alone does not settle its meaning.
Submit controlDelta.localExtractions:[{itemId,rules?,sourceBindings?,dependencies?,premiseValues?,policyRules?}]. Use op:add|replace,targetKey and the semantic fields of the corresponding local group, but OMIT questionId and evidenceIds inside these items: the host binds them to this offered WorkItem and actual current windows. It also supplies binding kind, origins and replacement digest. Keep after/from/parent as explicit current target keys; they express your proposed execution relationship, never lexical equality.
WorkItem.kind names a duty, not a rules.kind value. Principal-binding and resource-binding duties belong in sourceBindings with bindingKey and the appropriate bindingKind:principal or resource. The complete sourceBindings bindingKind enum is principal|resource|permission|configuration|value; rules.kind is entry|guard|reject|continue|effect. Use distinct targetKey values for distinct nodes across rules/sourceBindings. Reuse one typed principal/resource identity string for the same actual source object across bindings, guards and effects; use distinct identities for distinct objects. The host does not infer object aliases from prose or convert objects into identity strings.
Explain source conditions with the finite typed predicate algebra. Preserve owner=null separately from owner unspecified, missing grants separately from known false, and role exceptions. Check that claim text and typed predicate describe the same source branch before submitting. Source code does not supply a user premise. If a related source cannot be read, declare the dependency and its concrete gap rather than guessing.
Unknown premise entries are optional: normally omit them and keep the corresponding predicate binding unresolved. If submitting status:unspecified, text must be a verbatim span of the current question/premises, including its actual punctuation; do not paraphrase it. Prefer the default per-item update so an unrelated invalid span does not discard useful source interpretation. Request atomic:true only for a change that must succeed as one transaction.
A condition means THIS NODE IS REACHED. For source "if (!allowed) return deny; performEffect()", propose a reject terminal with condition allowed==false and an effect terminal with condition allowed==true on distinct pathKeys. Both conditions use wrapped operands. The effect follows the entry/bindings and any successful control, never the terminating reject. A guard reached on a failing condition cannot authorize its succeeding effect. Include explicit principal/resource binding nodes among the control/effect predecessors; identifying the same object in prose is insufficient.
An entry read does not close its called authorization helpers or upstream endpoint controls. Interpret the entry first, name decisive source dependencies, then interpret their actual windows and link the resulting conditions. Mark a terminal complete only after its relevant reachable controls and dependencies are examined. Policy pathKey must match the actual proposed behavior path, with expected outcome mapped from independent policy rather than source.
Unconfirmed lexical references are optional location leads, not compulsory explanation tasks. Link a dependency from the actual source rule when relevant to this question, or choose a shown candidate to inspect it. A unique same-name definition alone does not establish relevance or receiver identity.
Local explanation joins the next ordinary structured/native step. It does not create an extra provider request. You may still use ordinary changed control groups for already shown source outside an offered fragment. Invalid local items remain diagnosed while good siblings are retained, subject to the requested atomic update.
An interpreted source item remains editable until its question is checked. Amend existingTargets with op:replace when correcting the same source rule; a model reason may explain the change, otherwise the host records explicit local replacement provenance. Dependency relevance reasons remain required. Renaming a mistaken rule does not withdraw it. For an abandoned unaccepted draft, use root controlDelta.withdrawals with its exact group,questionId,targetKey and reason; accepted targets and missing links cannot be erased. After a stale local envelope rejection, use a currently offered task or a valid same-question ordinary update; specific rejected target diagnostics require correction or an explicit eligible withdrawal.
Domain feedback rejectedTargets shows at most four current rejected drafts with their exact group/question/target, submitted data, original local scope, diagnostics and archive pointer. Unaccepted targets require a corrected op:add under the same key; op:replace requires an accepted same-group target. A group conflict requires correcting the group or choosing a distinct key. Correct the fields named by diagnostics; pathKey, after, binding identity, conditions and completeness remain your explicit source interpretation. For local submission use only a CURRENTLY offered itemId and omit questionId/evidenceIds. Otherwise use the ordinary group with the recorded questionId and actually shown evidenceIds. If abandoning an eligible unaccepted draft, explicitly withdraw its exact identity with a reason. Renaming alone leaves the failure active. Large drafts are omitted as a whole with an archive pointer, never silently truncated or filled.
Deferred tasks are not current local offers. Whole original windows are selected within sourceBudget; no source lines or semantic fields are summarized. Previously shown evidence remains referenceable through the catalog and ordinary updates. A candidateRefinement location task offers the SAME indexed alternatives for an incompletely read entry; choose a narrower candidate only when it identifies this requested entry. The host does not change that choice or infer relevance.
A source binding's bindingKey declares its typed identity; principal/resource fields reference that bindingKey. For example bindingKind:principal,bindingKey:visitor declares visitor, and a downstream principal:visitor references it. On that binding node omit its own principal or repeat principal:visitor; principal:anotherName does not declare an alias. Use different typed identity keys for different objects even if labels/IDs match. authorizedBy asserts that a particular guard controls THIS effect on the same principal/resource; omit the assertion if no such linkage is established, and explain source-visible missing control rather than inventing a guard. Do not assume a checked input object also authorizes an output object.
Predicates support only {op:eq|neq,left:{binding:name}|{literal:scalar},right:{binding:name}|{literal:scalar}}, {op:is-null,value:{binding:name}|{literal:scalar}}, {op:all|any,args:[predicates]}, {op:not,arg:predicate}; scalar is string/number/boolean/null. BOTH operands must be wrapped, for example {op:"eq",left:{binding:"flag"},right:{literal:false}}; bare right:false is invalid. Max depth12/nodes64. No target code, arbitrary operator or natural text is evaluated. Only known premiseValues from exact current user spans enter evaluation; mapping meaning remains unreviewed. For an unspecified/unknown/not-given value OMIT the binding completely and refer to its key only in predicates; NEVER use value:null or value:false as an unknown placeholder. null is valid only when the current user explicitly supplies a null premise. Represent source outcomes with rules/conditions, do not invent user binding values from source.

Place a dependency after a reject only if source order actually makes it unreachable. Policy mappings are separate candidates: {op,targetKey,questionId,pathKey,expected:allow|deny,origin:policy,text:<exact policy span>,location:<current independent location>,condition?}. Map only the supplied policy, do not derive it from implementation. Each live path needs a mapping for a determined policy assessment; incomplete mappings remain undetermined while behavior is deliverable. Formal policy mapping is still unreviewed.
For unspecified values, retain alternative feasible outcomes and name the missing fact. Local extraction and mapping meaning remain unreviewed.

Use kind:control with controlDelta to propose just changed rules/dependencies; controlDelta is also optional on another step. Host returns actual new source in the next response context. Propose dependencies promptly instead of choosing every helper read yourself.

Each item has op:add|replace, questionId, targetKey. Replace names the current same-question target; a model reason is optional for ordinary items, and the host records explicit replacement provenance and revisionOf. Dependency reason remains required to explain source relevance. baseRevision detects a stale view. atomic:true applies the submitted group or none: its own or newly broken predecessor/dependency links cause rollback; unrelated unchanged gaps remain visible without rolling back this transaction. Rejected items and their dependent gaps remain visible; correct only diagnosed items.
To abandon a malformed UNACCEPTED draft, submit withdrawals:[{group:rules|sourceBindings|dependencies|premiseValues|policyRules,questionId,targetKey,reason}]. This retires only that exact draft's current rejection, preserving its original proposal and the withdrawal reason. It never deletes an accepted target, another group's error, source invalidation or missing predecessor/dependency gaps. Failed atomic updates apply no withdrawals. Renaming a draft alone does not withdraw it.
rules are entry/guard/reject/continue/effect with pathKey,after,evidenceIds,claim and optional finite condition/principal/resource/operation/authorizedBy/complete. sourceBindings are source identities with pathKey,after,evidenceIds,claim,bindingKey,bindingKind; the host sets kind:binding. A source identity is never a user value.
A new entry with omitted after declares a root (after:[]). Explicit entry predecessors stay unchanged. Replacements and all other rule kinds require after; a missing predecessor must never be guessed. Final observations may be omitted when there are no additional observations.
premiseValues are explicit user facts: {op,questionId,targetKey,status:known,value,text:<exact original user span>} or {op,questionId,targetKey,status:unspecified,text}. Unspecified has NO value field; it does not mean null or false. Omit unspecified items if no update is needed. Policy mappings stay in policyRules, with expected,text,location and optional condition; the host sets origin:policy.
For a shown ambiguous WorkItem submit workSelections:[{questionId,itemId,candidateId}] using its shown candidate ID. This is a lexical read choice, not an authorization fact or a closed-state declaration. Atomic applies to the control update groups; location choices are separate read intents.
Current locationTasks contain unlocated WorkItems or optional unconfirmed lexical references from interpreted parent source, not source interpretations. For locate use ordinary source_search/source_symbol/source_read to establish an original location. A location task does not authorize localExtractions until its actual read window is offered as an explanation task. Resolve decisive locations alongside already-read explanation tasks; unresolved decisive locations cannot be skipped as completed questions. Optional lexical leads need not apply.
Current local explanation tasks are executable duties: interpret the offered WorkItem using its original sourceWindows and current question/premises. A read/citation alone does not settle its meaning.
Submit controlDelta.localExtractions:[{itemId,rules?,sourceBindings?,dependencies?,premiseValues?,policyRules?}]. Use op:add|replace,targetKey and the semantic fields of the corresponding local group, but OMIT questionId and evidenceIds inside these items: the host binds them to this offered WorkItem and actual current windows. It also supplies binding kind, origins and replacement digest. Keep after/from/parent as explicit current target keys; they express your proposed execution relationship, never lexical equality.
WorkItem.kind names a duty, not a rules.kind value. Principal-binding and resource-binding duties belong in sourceBindings with bindingKey and the appropriate bindingKind:principal or resource. The complete sourceBindings bindingKind enum is principal|resource|permission|configuration|value; rules.kind is entry|guard|reject|continue|effect. Use distinct targetKey values for distinct nodes across rules/sourceBindings. Reuse one typed principal/resource identity string for the same actual source object across bindings, guards and effects; use distinct identities for distinct objects. The host does not infer object aliases from prose or convert objects into identity strings.

A condition means THIS NODE IS REACHED. For source "if (!allowed) return deny; performEffect()", propose a reject terminal with condition allowed==false and an effect terminal with condition allowed==true on distinct pathKeys. Both conditions use wrapped operands. The effect follows the entry/bindings and any successful control, never the terminating reject. A guard reached on a failing condition cannot authorize its succeeding effect. Include explicit principal/resource binding nodes among the control/effect predecessors; identifying the same object in prose is insufficient.
An entry read does not close its called authorization helpers or upstream endpoint controls. Interpret the entry first, name decisive source dependencies, then interpret their actual windows and link the resulting conditions. Mark a terminal complete only after its relevant reachable controls and dependencies are examined. Policy pathKey must match the actual proposed behavior path, with expected outcome mapped from independent policy rather than source.
Unconfirmed lexical references are optional location leads, not compulsory explanation tasks. Link a dependency from the actual source rule when relevant to this question, or choose a shown candidate to inspect it. A unique same-name definition alone does not establish relevance or receiver identity.

A source binding's bindingKey declares its typed identity; principal/resource fields reference that bindingKey. For example bindingKind:principal,bindingKey:visitor declares visitor, and a downstream principal:visitor references it. On that binding node omit its own principal or repeat principal:visitor; principal:anotherName does not declare an alias. Use different typed identity keys for different objects even if labels/IDs match. authorizedBy asserts that a particular guard controls THIS effect on the same principal/resource; omit the assertion if no such linkage is established, and explain source-visible missing control rather than inventing a guard. Do not assume a checked input object also authorizes an output object.
Predicates support only {op:eq|neq,left:{binding:name}|{literal:scalar},right:{binding:name}|{literal:scalar}}, {op:is-null,value:{binding:name}|{literal:scalar}}, {op:all|any,args:[predicates]}, {op:not,arg:predicate}; scalar is string/number/boolean/null. BOTH operands must be wrapped, for example {op:"eq",left:{binding:"flag"},right:{literal:false}}; bare right:false is invalid. Max depth12/nodes64. No target code, arbitrary operator or natural text is evaluated. Only known premiseValues from exact current user spans enter evaluation; mapping meaning remains unreviewed. For an unspecified/unknown/not-given value OMIT the binding completely and refer to its key only in predicates; NEVER use value:null or value:false as an unknown placeholder. null is valid only when the current user explicitly supplies a null premise. Represent source outcomes with rules/conditions, do not invent user binding values from source.

Policy mappings are separate candidates: {op,targetKey,questionId,pathKey,expected:allow|deny,origin:policy,text:<exact policy span>,location:<current independent location>,condition?}.         # Run async embedding in sync context using the main event loop
        # This allows the main loop to stay responsive to health checks during long operations
        embedding_timeout = RAG_EMBEDDING_TIMEOUT

        future = asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(
            embedding_function(
                list(map(lambda x: x.replace('\n', ' '), texts)),
                prefix=RAG_EMBEDDING_CONTENT_PREFIX,
                user=user,
            ),
            request.app.state.main_loop,
        )
        embeddings = future.result(timeout=embedding_timeout)
        log.info(f'embeddings generated {len(embeddings)} for {len(texts)} items')

        items = [
            {
                'id': str(uuid.uuid4()),
                'text': text,
                'vector': embeddings[idx],
                'metadata': metadatas[idx],
            }
            for idx, text in enumerate(texts)
        ]

        log.info(f'adding to collection {collection_name}')
        VECTOR_DB_CLIENT.insert(
            collection_name=collection_name,
            items=items,
        )

        log.info(f'added {len(items)} items to collection {collection_name}')
        return True
    except Exception as e:
        log.exception(e)
        raise e

rules.claim: POST /process/file receives form_data, a verified user, and a database session; it chooses the file lookup by user.role, then processes the selected file and may update it and save documents to a collection.

For an admin caller, the endpoint calls get_file_by_id with the supplied file_id; the helper performs a database lookup by that ID and returns the file model if found, without a caller-user ownership predicate in the shown helper.
For a non-admin caller, the file lookup filters simultaneously by the supplied file id and the caller's user id; it returns that matching file or None, and catches lookup exceptions as None.
rules.operation: lookup file by supplied id constrained to caller id

rules.claim: If the selected file lookup yields no file, the endpoint terminates with HTTP 404 NOT_FOUND and does not reach processing or vector persistence.
If the selected file exists, execution enters the processing branch and chooses collection_name from form_data or derives file-{file.id} when it is absent.
Before the embedding/vector-save branch completes, the endpoint updates the selected file's content by file.id; later success or failure updates also target that same file.id.

When embedding/retrieval is not bypassed, the endpoint commits pending file changes and calls save_docs_to_vector_db with the caller, the selected destination collection_name, documents carrying the selected file_id in metadata, and add true only when collection_name was supplied.
rules.operation: save_docs_to_vector_db(docs, collection_name, metadata={file_id, name, hash}, add=(form_data.collection_name is not None), user=caller)

rules.claim: When BYPASS_EMBEDDING_AND_RETRIEVAL is enabled, the endpoint updates the selected file to completed and records its hash, then returns success without the shown vector-save call.
get_verified_user rejects roles outside user and admin with HTTP 401 and otherwise returns the current user object used by process_file as user.

For the non-admin lookup, get_file_by_id_and_user_id selects a file only when both the supplied id and the supplied user_id match the database row; it returns the validated file model or None, and catches lookup exceptions as None.

The destination resource is the request's form_data.collection_name when supplied, otherwise the endpoint derives file-{file.id}; the shown endpoint passes collection_name to vector-database operations and does not perform a destination-owner check here.

The vector helper queries the destination collection for the supplied content hash; if a matching document exists, it permits re-add only when the existing document metadata file_id equals the selected file.id, and otherwise raises a duplicate-content error.

The vector helper checks whether the destination collection exists; an existing collection with add false returns success without inserting, while add true permits the subsequent embedding and insert path.

On the non-duplicate path, after collection handling and embedding generation, the helper inserts the generated vector items into the caller-supplied destination collection_name; the inserted metadata includes the selected file_id, filename and content hash.

Exceptions from vector saving propagate back to the route's outer handler, which updates the selected file status to failed and clears its hash before returning an HTTP 400-style error; this is a file-side failure update, not destination authorization.

        # Run async embedding in sync context using the main event loop
        # This allows the main loop to stay responsive to health checks during long operations
        embedding_timeout = RAG_EMBEDDING_TIMEOUT

        future = asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(
            embedding_function(
                list(map(lambda x: x.replace('\n', ' '), texts)),
                prefix=RAG_EMBEDDING_CONTENT_PREFIX,
                user=user,
            ),
            request.app.state.main_loop,
        )
        embeddings = future.result(timeout=embedding_timeout)
        log.info(f'embeddings generated {len(embeddings)} for {len(texts)} items')

        items = [
            {
                'id': str(uuid.uuid4()),
                'text': text,
                'vector': embeddings[idx],
                'metadata': metadatas[idx],
            }
            for idx, text in enumerate(texts)
        ]

        log.info(f'adding to collection {collection_name}')
        VECTOR_DB_CLIENT.insert(
            collection_name=collection_name,
            items=items,
        )

        log.info(f'added {len(items)} items to collection {collection_name}')
        return True
    except Exception as e:
        log.exception(e)
        raise e

        # Run async embedding in sync context using the main event loop
        # This allows the main loop to stay responsive to health checks during long operations
        embedding_timeout = RAG_EMBEDDING_TIMEOUT

        future = asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(

                'text': text,
                'vector': embeddings[idx],
                'metadata': metadatas[idx],
            }
            for idx, text in enumerate(texts)

            items=items,

        log.info(f'added {len(items)} items to collection {collection_name}')

rules.claim: POST /process/file receives form_data, a verified user, and a database session; it chooses the file lookup by user.role, then processes the selected file and may update it and save documents to a collection.

For an admin caller, the endpoint calls get_file_by_id with the supplied file_id; the helper performs a database lookup by that ID and returns the file model if found, without a caller-user ownership predicate in the shown helper.
For a non-admin caller, the file lookup filters simultaneously by the supplied file id and the caller's user id; it returns that matching file or None, and catches lookup exceptions as None.
rules.operation: lookup file by supplied id constrained to caller id

rules.claim: If the selected file lookup yields no file, the endpoint terminates with HTTP 404 NOT_FOUND and does not reach processing or vector persistence.
If the selected file exists, execution enters the processing branch and chooses collection_name from form_data or derives file-{file.id} when it is absent.
Before the embedding/vector-save branch completes, the endpoint updates the selected file's content by file.id; later success or failure updates also target that same file.id.

When embedding/retrieval is not bypassed, the endpoint commits pending file changes and calls save_docs_to_vector_db with the caller, the selected destination collection_name, documents carrying the selected file_id in metadata, and add true only when collection_name was supplied.
rules.operation: save_docs_to_vector_db(docs, collection_name, metadata={file_id, name, hash}, add=(form_data.collection_name is not None), user=caller)

rules.claim: When BYPASS_EMBEDDING_AND_RETRIEVAL is enabled, the endpoint updates the selected file to completed and records its hash, then returns success without the shown vector-save call.
get_verified_user rejects roles outside user and admin with HTTP 401 and otherwise returns the current user object used by process_file as user.

For the non-admin lookup, get_file_by_id_and_user_id selects a file only when both the supplied id and the supplied user_id match the database row; it returns the validated file model or None, and catches lookup exceptions as None.

The destination resource is the request's form_data.collection_name when supplied, otherwise the endpoint derives file-{file.id}; the shown endpoint passes collection_name to vector-database operations and does not perform a destination-owner check here.

The vector helper queries the destination collection for the supplied content hash; if a matching document exists, it permits re-add only when the existing document metadata file_id equals the selected file.id, and otherwise raises a duplicate-content error.

The vector helper checks whether the destination collection exists; an existing collection with add false returns success without inserting, while add true permits the subsequent embedding and insert path.

On the non-duplicate path, after collection handling and embedding generation, the helper inserts the generated vector items into the caller-supplied destination collection_name; the inserted metadata includes the selected file_id, filename and content hash.

Exceptions from vector saving propagate back to the route's outer handler, which updates the selected file status to failed and clears its hash before returning an HTTP 400-style error; this is a file-side failure update, not destination authorization.

behavior.explanation: The endpoint first obtains a verified caller, then selects the input file by file_id. An admin uses an id-only lookup; a non-admin uses an id-plus-caller-user-id lookup. A missing selected file produces HTTP 404 before processing.
